local_facts.title: Public-entity injury claims have an early notice rule
local_facts.claim: California Government Code section 911.2 states that a claim relating to injury to a person must generally be presented no later than six months after the cause of action accrues.
local_facts.why_it_matters: An injury involving a Modesto-area city, county, school, park, sidewalk, or other public entity may need prompt agency identification and claim-presentment review rather than an ordinary wait-and-see insurance approach.

local_facts.title: Agriculture and food manufacturing shape local work-injury questions
local_facts.claim: Stanislaus County reported that agriculture supported 29,192 direct employees in 2017; a Caltrans Stanislaus County forecast states food and beverage processing accounted for 47 percent of the county’s manufacturing employment.
local_facts.why_it_matters: A significant share of local injuries may happen in work settings, where Labor Code section 3602 generally makes workers’ compensation the exclusive remedy against an employer when its conditions apply; the employment relationship and any other parties must be identified before choosing a claim path.

local_facts.title: Stanislaus County civil court is in downtown Modesto
local_facts.claim: The Superior Court of California, County of Stanislaus lists City Towers Courthouse (Civil) at 801 10th Street in Modesto, with civil departments and the Civil Clerk’s Office in the building.
local_facts.why_it_matters: A dispute that proceeds beyond an agency claim process is handled through a defined local civil court structure, not through a generic claims office.

pricing.table_head: Three separate questions in a Stanislaus County injury claim: the fee standard, the caps on other case types, and the clerk's amounts

anchors.label: Number California puts on a negligence fee
anchors.detail: The governing rule bars an unconscionable or illegal fee and then lists thirteen circumstances for evaluating one. A percentage for injury work appears nowhere in it.
anchors.source_name: Cal. Rules of Prof. Conduct, rule 1.5(a)

anchors.label: First paper where the claim runs above $10,000 to $35,000
anchors.detail: Taken from the civil fee schedule the Stanislaus County Superior Court posts for filings in Modesto, and charged again on the answering party's first paper.
anchors.source_name: Stanislaus County Superior Court civil fee schedule, item 7

anchors.label: Court reporting for a civil hearing of an hour or less
anchors.detail: Beyond an hour the schedule switches to a per diem of $700 for a full day or $350 for a half day, charged for each reporter the proceeding requires.
anchors.source_name: Stanislaus County Superior Court civil fee schedule, item 66

anchors.label: Ceiling on a hospital lien against a settlement
anchors.detail: That limit governs how much a hospital lien can pull out of a judgment or settlement after prior liens are paid. It is a limit on the hospital, not on a fee.

fee_rows.stage: Fee in a Modesto negligence claim
fee_rows.note: Reviewed against thirteen listed circumstances, including whether material facts went undisclosed, the proportion between fee and the value of services, and whether informed consent was given.
fee_rows.source_name: Cal. Rules of Prof. Conduct, rule 1.5(b)

fee_rows.stage: Professional negligence against a health care provider
fee_rows.note: A medical negligence schedule and nothing broader, computed on the sum recovered after disbursements, with higher rates allowed only on a good-cause motion.

fee_rows.share: Amount fixed by the appeals board
fee_rows.note: The board approves or sets the figure before any fee may be demanded or accepted from the injured worker, weighing responsibility assumed, care exercised, time involved and results.

fee_rows.stage: Contingency contract missing a required statement
fee_rows.note: Once voided, the attorney may collect a reasonable fee instead of the contract share, which is why the required disclosures deserve reading at signature.

fee_rows.stage: Reclassifying a limited case as unlimited
fee_rows.note: Filed when discovery shows the claim exceeds the limited jurisdiction ceiling, while an amendment that raises the amount at issue within the same tier is $145.
fee_rows.source_name: Stanislaus County Superior Court civil fee schedule, item 15

fee_rows.note: Any paper requiring a hearing draws the first amount, while a summary judgment or summary adjudication motion draws the second.
fee_rows.source_name: Stanislaus County Superior Court civil fee schedule, items 45 and 51
